<section class="component info-text-block    [ mb-40 ml-1/10 mr-1/10 ] [ md:w-14/20 md:mb-50 md:ml-5/20 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:w-13/20 lg:mb-60 ] js-component" id="info-text-block-107296" data-component="info-text-block">
    <div class="container">
        <div class="info-text-block__container [ md:flex md:flex-row md:items-start ] ">
      <div class="info-text-block__intro [ block mb-20 font-tiempos text-16 leading-23 text-red ] [ lg:mb-30 lg:text-22 lg:leading-27 ]">We provide medical and psychological assistance to people affected by the ongoing conflict in the West Bank and Gaza.  </div>      <div class="info-text-block__content">
          <p>In Gaza, the local healthcare system is overstretched, underfunded and deeply impacted by a 16-year blockade. We provide assistance to people affected by burns and trauma with a multi-disciplinary approach, which can include <a data-entity-substitution="canonical" data-entity-type="taxonomy_term" data-entity-uuid="f142bf80-4f2c-48c9-9c9f-a1840d72b236" href="/surgery-trauma-care">surgical care</a>, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, health education, and psychosocial support. <br>
 <br>
In the West Bank, occupation, violence, unemployment and poverty continue to have a profound impact on the <a data-entity-substitution="canonical" data-entity-type="taxonomy_term" data-entity-uuid="9364442a-8275-4705-a41f-9837f1b06027" href="/mental-health">mental health</a> of Palestinians. Our teams offer psychological support in Hebron, Nablus, and Qalqilya. <br>
<br>
We provide healthcare services in H2 area, in Hebron city, where Palestinian residents’ movements are subject to restrictions that severely impede their access to healthcare. We also started running mobile clinics to address the health needs of communities in Masafer Yatta, who are facing home demolitions and an increased risk of forcible transfer.</p>

                  </div><!-- /.info-text-block__content -->    </div><!-- /.info-text-block__container -->

<div class="expandable-block toolkit [ ml-1/10 mr-1/10 ] [ md:pt-48 md:ml-6/20 ] [ lg:ml-5/20 lg:w-11/20 ] js-expandable-block" id="expandable-block-295549">
    <div class="expandable-block__extended" id="expandable-block-295549-content" aria-hidden="true" style="display: none;"><p><strong>Gaza</strong> <br>In 2025, Israel continued its ruthless campaign in Gaza, not only through brutal and incessant violence, but also through months of blockade, denying people their most basic needs for survival, such as food and water, culminating in famine conditions in some areas in August. By 31 December, 71,266 people had been killed by Israeli forces since the start of the war,* while civilian infrastructure and the health system in the Gaza Strip had been systematically decimated. <br><br>Throughout the year, Palestinians were forcibly displaced and pushed into an ever-shrinking geographic area. MSF teams supporting emergency departments responded to multiple mass-casualty incidents, receiving hundreds of patients killed or injured by Israeli strikes in southern Gaza. We also witnessed how the Israeli authorities increasingly suppressed humanitarian space, including by dismantling the UN-led response and replacing it with a militarised food distribution scheme run by the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF). This led to violence and <a href="https://www.msf.org/dozens-palestinians-massacred-us-israel-backed-food-distribution-sites">killings at food distribution sites</a>. MSF’s clinics were overwhelmed by patients with gunshot wounds, lacerations, and crush injuries, many of them children, as people were shot at or injured in the chaos as they tried to get food. Across the Strip, our teams treated a growing number of children with moderate and severe malnutrition until the <a href="https://www.msf.org/ceasefire-gaza-humanitarian-aid-must-flow-immediately">ceasefire came into effect on 10 October</a>.  <br><br>MSF called on the Israeli authorities to end the violence, allow humanitarian aid to enter at scale, and dismantle the GHF sites (which stopped functioning after the October ceasefire). Meanwhile, the Israeli authorities introduced a new registration system for international NGOs with restrictive and politicised rules, <a href="https://www.msf.org/msfs-vital-humanitarian-activities-gaza-risk-israeli-registration-rules">fundamentally jeopardising the continuation of humanitarian action</a> in Palestine. <br><br>At the end of August, the Israeli forces launched a large-scale offensive on Gaza City, destroying entire neighbourhoods and forcibly displacing hundreds of thousands of people into the middle of the Strip. As a result, MSF had no option but to relocate teams and <a href="https://www.msf.org/msf-forced-suspend-activities-amid-israeli-offensive-gaza-city">suspend all medical activities in the city at the end of September</a>. <br><br>After a second ceasefire came into effect in October, Palestinians returned to the north, and MSF teams relaunched activities. We returned to public hospitals, resuming paediatric services, burns treatment, and physiotherapy, and helping to repair facilities that were filled with rubble. We also opened multiple medical points to deliver general healthcare in areas where the Israeli forces had destroyed all the health facilities. In spite of the ceasefire, the flow of humanitarian aid into Gaza remained critically inadequate, and Israel continued to block essential items, such as shelter materials and so-called dual use items,** exacerbating the dire winter living conditions. <br><br>In response to the immense needs, we expanded our medical and water and sanitation activities throughout the year. MSF continued to be one of the largest providers of services such as comprehensive care for patients with burns and trauma injuries, which included physiotherapy, dressing wounds, surgery, and maternal and neonatal healthcare. By the end of the year, our teams were supporting six hospitals and seven healthcare centres. We were also running two field hospitals, two clinics, and an inpatient feeding centre, as well as providing clean water to hundreds of thousands of Palestinians in Gaza. <br><br>In 2025, six more MSF colleagues died in Israeli airstrikes or targeted attacks, taking the <a href="https://www.msf.org/remembering-our-colleagues-killed-gaza">total number of MSF staff killed in Gaza</a> to 15. To date, our official request for an independent investigation into these killings has not officially been answered by the Israeli authorities. We have made repeated calls for a sustained and immediate ceasefire, urgent and unhindered access for humanitarian aid, medical evacuations, and an end to the genocide. <br><br><strong>The West Bank</strong> <br>In the West Bank, MSF teams continued to witness the consequences of policies and <a href="https://www.msf.org/msf-teams-see-risk-ethnic-cleansing-west-bank">practices of ethnic cleansing</a>, aimed at forcibly transferring Palestinians from their land and preventing any possibility of return. This included a sharp increase in violence by the Israeli military and settlers, who killed and injured many Palestinians. While not new, we witnessed a clear expansion of Israeli settlements and policies aimed at displacing Palestinians in 2025. The ongoing Israeli Iron Wall military operation, which began in January 2025, forcibly displaced 40,000 people in the northern West Bank within a month, according to UNRWA, the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees.*** Three refugee camps were violently raided and emptied. <a href="https://www.msf.org/west-bank-homes-masafer-yatta-communities-have-been-reduced-rubble">Homes and civilian infrastructure</a> ⁠– including schools and healthcare centres ⁠– were demolished, increasing the likelihood that the displacement will become permanent. MSF operated mobile clinics to deliver general healthcare to thousands of people displaced by the military operations in the north, particularly in Jenin and Tulkarem, and distributed hygiene kits, food parcels, and clean water. <br><br>In Hebron, Nablus, Qalqilya, and Tubas, our operations focused on offering medical and mental health support to people affected by settler attacks, demolitions, and displacement, through both mobile and fixed clinics. The constant fear regarding longer and unpredictable incursions and attacks by both Israeli forces and settlers is taking a significant toll on people’s mental health, increasing feelings of hopelessness and anxiety, as observed by our mental health teams. MSF also conducted training for Palestinian Red Crescent Society volunteers, and supported healthcare facilities with training and donations of supplies, including water and fuel. <br><br><strong>MSF’s registration beyond 2025 </strong><br>Throughout the year, MSF faced severe operational uncertainty, due to Israel’s attempts to control and restrict the activities of humanitarian organisations by demanding they re-register to work in the country and submit private information about Palestinian staff. MSF had considerable and legitimate concerns about sharing this data, and therefore, in August, we provided all information requested, except personal details of our staff, which we refused to provide to the Israeli authorities without guaranteed safeguards. Without registration, which expired on 31 December, MSF is unable to send supplies or international staff into Palestine, but our Palestinian teams remain committed to providing assistance for as long as possible.</p><h5><br><br>*United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA): <a href="https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-update-351-gaza-strip" class="ext" data-extlink="" target="_blank" rel="noopener" title="(opens in a new window)">https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-update-351-gaza-strip</a><br>**A dual-use item is a product, material, or technology that is intended for legitimate civilian or medical use, but is blocked or restricted from entering the Gaza Strip by Israeli authorities because it could potentially be repurposed for military use. <br>***UNRWA: <a href="https://www.unrwa.org/newsroom/official-statements/large-scale-forced-displacement-west-bank-impacts-40000-people " class="ext" data-extlink="" target="_blank" rel="noopener" title="(opens in a new window)">https://www.unrwa.org/newsroom/official-statements/large-scale-forced-displacement-west-bank-impacts-40000-people </a> <br>     </h5></div>

<section class="fc-intro-section">

    <div class="column small-12 medium-7">
      <h3>Gaza’s 2.1 million civilians are facing a major humanitarian crisis. Violence across the Gaza Strip has displaced more than 90% of the population, leaving them with limited access to healthcare, food, water and other essential services.</h3>
<p><span class="s1">International Medical Corps has provided lifesaving humanitarian assistance and protection services in Gaza since 2008, focusing on emergency preparedness, coordination and delivery of primary and secondary healthcare, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), child protection (CP), nutrition, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, as well as services to address violence against women and girls (VAWG).</span></p>
<p>International Medical Corps has provided lifesaving humanitarian assistance and protection services in Gaza since 2008, focusing on emergency preparedness, coordination and delivery of primary and secondary healthcare, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), child protection (CP), nutrition, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, as well as services to address violence against women and girls (VAWG).</p>
<p>We have deployed fully equipped field hospitals, and work with international and local partners to implement vaccination and malnutrition campaigns to help children throughout Gaza.</p>

<section class="fc-list_content-block ">

  
      <div class="fc-section-title">
      <h2>Our Response</h2>
    </div>
  

            <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Survivor-Care.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <p>The ever-changing security situation and ongoing tensions compound the challenges of humanitarian response in Gaza. Before the conflict escalated in 2023, our work focused on implementing emergency preparedness and coordination projects, and on providing primary and secondary healthcare, MHPSS, CP, and services to address VAWG.</p>
<p>Following the conflict’s escalation, we adapted our services to meet the dire humanitarian needs of Gazan civilians, including establishing large, fully functional field hospitals to provide civilians with surgical and trauma services, outpatient services, MHPSS, CP, nutrition and WASH services.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Emergency-Response-Preparedness-1.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Primary and Secondary Healthcare</h3>
                        <p>Our field hospitals and multi-purpose centers together provide comprehensive primary healthcare services—including outpatient consultations, disease prevention and treatment, routine immunizations, and maternal and newborn healthcare—to displaced populations across Gaza. The hospitals are classified as Level 4 primary healthcare centers.</p>
<p>Our hospital in central Gaza focuses primarily on internal medicine and on comprehensive maternal and newborn health services. It has an emergency room, an operating theater and a neonatal intensive-care unit (NICU), supported by a laboratory, a pharmacy, a blood bank and a radiology department.</p>
<p>Our field hospitals in the north provide comprehensive medical services focused on trauma care, patient rehabilitation, surgeries and maternity care, offering operating rooms, an intensive care unit and a NICU. The hospitals also offer physiotherapy, integrated protection and nutrition services.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Nutrition-2.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Nutrition</h3>
                        <p>We provide integrated nutrition services through 10 sites at the community and facility levels. These services include malnutrition screening, outpatient therapeutic programs, targeted supplementary-feeding programs, blanket supplementary-feeding programs, infant and young-child feeding (IYCF) programs and a stabilization center.</p>
<p>Regular screening enables early identification and treatment of acute malnutrition. We provide clinical nutrition support to pediatric and adult inpatients through assessments, therapeutic nutrition plans, counseling and monitoring. Our IYCF programming includes counseling, support groups, cooking demonstrations and mother-baby spaces that promote safe infant-feeding practices. We also provide therapeutic and ready-to-eat meals to inpatients.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Water-Sanitation-Hygiene-1.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Water, Sanitation and Hygiene</h3>
                        <p>Our technical experts lead the design, construction and maintenance of critical WASH infrastructure, including reliable water-supply systems with desalination and backup units; accessible sanitation facilities, such as toilets, showers and handwashing stations; and comprehensive waste-management systems that cover medical and general waste through segregation and safe disposal, following strict infection-prevention and control standards.</p>
<p>We raise awareness of handwashing, safe-waste storage and waterborne-disease prevention through hygiene-promotion activities. During emergencies, we deliver safe water to displaced communities through multiple distribution points—ensuring safe, dignified and continuous care in challenging environments.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Mental-Health-Psychosocial-Support.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Mental Health and Psychosocial Support</h3>
                        <p>Our MHPSS work strengthens social connections and promotes positive coping strategies through comprehensive, multi-tiered MHPSS services aligned with the Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) pyramid and the World Health Organization’s Mental Health Gap Action Programme. We provide MHPSS services through a multidisciplinary team of psychiatrists, psychologists and psychosocial workers who support those experiencing distress, as well as mental, neurological and substance-use conditions.</p>
<p>We use tools such as Self-Help Plus as well as peer-support activities in group sessions to strengthen coping skills and build social connections. In our hospitals and through outreach, our community prevention and promotion activities include psychoeducation, stigma reduction, healing ceremonies and awareness sessions. We help local healthcare workers, volunteers and partner organizations integrate MHPSS into existing systems.</p>
<p>We have established the first inpatient center for mental health—called the Acute Psychiatric Stabilization Unit—in central Gaza to provide specialized psychiatric care and mental health services to people experiencing psychological distress.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Challenges_Children’s-Health-3.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Child Protection</h3>
                        <p>Since establishing our field hospitals, we have expanded our CP interventions to include structured and unstructured psychosocial activities in our child-friendly space. The CP team provides case management, counseling, psychological first aid (PFA), and parenting and awareness sessions to build resilience and strengthen coping.</p>
<p>Children in inpatient care receive daily psychosocial support, including during medical procedures. Our team also supports unaccompanied and separated children by providing structured case management. Our comprehensive approach helps to reduce CP risks and ensure a safe, supportive environment that upholds children’s rights and dignity.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Challenges_Gender-based-violence.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Violence Against Women and Girls</h3>
                        <p>Recognizing the needs of women and girls at risk of violence in conflict-affected settings, we provide information sessions, PFA, individual support sessions and targeted interventions to educate the community on how to recognize, prevent and report VAWG. We connect survivors to medical care and psychosocial support through specialized case management.</p>
<p>To provide holistic assistance, we integrate all protection services with medical care. Our teams coordinate referrals internally and externally, and provide protection training for our staff and partners.</p>
<p>To further support women and girls, we operate women’s and girls’ safe spaces (WGSSs) that offer safe environments for information-sharing, social support and skills training. Our WGSS activities build resilience, promote well-being and reduce the risk of VAWG through survivor-centered programming.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

                <p>Food insecurity was already widespread in Gaza prior to the escalation of conflict on October 7, 2023. 			<script>
				// Used by Gallery Custom Links to handle tenacious Lightboxes.
				//
				// 2026/08/15: Until now this walked the DOM on load and set onclick = null on
				// the images. That only ever removed handlers assigned as an onclick *property*,
				// so every lightbox binding through addEventListener survived it: jQuery ones,
				// delegated ones, and WordPress core's own "Expand on click" (the Interactivity
				// API binds data-wp-on--click on the img, and its showLightbox() calls neither
				// preventDefault nor stopPropagation). The lightbox opened and the link was
				// followed at the same time, or the lightbox swallowed the click entirely.
				//
				// One listener on window in the capture phase fixes all of them at once: capture
				// runs from the top of the tree down, so we see the click before anything bound
				// on the image itself and can stop it from ever getting there. We deliberately do
				// NOT preventDefault, which leaves the browser to follow the link on its own, so
				// target, ctrl/cmd-click and middle-click all keep behaving natively. Being
				// delegated, it also covers galleries added to the page after load (AJAX,
				// infinite scroll), which the old load-time pass never saw.
				window.addEventListener('click', function (ev) {
					if (!ev.target || !ev.target.closest) {
						return;
					}
					if (!ev.target.closest('a.no-lightbox, a.set-target')) {
						return;
					}
					ev.stopPropagation();
					if (ev.stopImmediatePropagation) {
						ev.stopImmediatePropagation();
					}
				}, true);
			</script>

Gaza continues to endure an ongoing humanitarian catastrophe. During two years of hostilities, the majority of the population was displaced and tens of thousands of Palestinians killed.
Updated 22. Sep 2026
Palestine

Despite a ceasefire agreement reached in October 2025, the situation remains critical, with frequent Israeli strikes, severe supply shortages and restrictions blocking humanitarian access and assistance.

In addition to Gaza, the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is facing a displacement and protection crisis. Israeli military operations, government-backed settler violence, demolitions, forced evictions and settlement expansion continue to uproot Palestinian families and further destabilise the region. Despite the challenges, the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is continuing with its efforts to save lives, protect rights and ease suffering.  

What’s happening in Palestine?

In October 2023, attacks by Palestinian armed groups resulted in the deaths of approximately 1,200 Israelis and foreign nationals, with over 250 people taken hostage. In response, Israel launched devastating strikes on Gaza, leaving entire communities in ruins. Widespread destruction of homes and infrastructure displaced at least 1.9 million people – around 90 per cent of Gaza’s population. Many families, including the small percentage who were able to return, remain without safe shelter or access to basic services. 

The ongoing siege and restrictions on humanitarian access have resulted in critical shortages of food, clean water, shelter and medical supplies that put countless lives at risk. Although a ceasefire agreement was reached in October 2025, severe humanitarian access constraints remain, and the risk of renewed hostilities continues. 

The West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is facing its largest and most prolonged displacement crisis since 1967. Violence continues to rise, with Israeli settler attacks increasing in frequency and intensity alongside expanding settlement activity, land appropriation and forced displacement. Intensified Israeli military operations in the northern West Bank displaced tens of thousands of Palestinians from refugee camps, leaving many people in an increasingly vulnerable situation. 

Across the occupied Palestinian territory, bureaucratic restrictions, logistical barriers and the closure of crossings and checkpoints continue to delay or block life-saving assistance.  

Urgent international action is needed to prevent further loss of life, ensure safe humanitarian access and uphold the rights of Palestinians. 

Our response

We’re working with our partners in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, in the following areas:

  • Water, sanitation and hygiene – expanding access to safe drinking water, sanitation facilities and hygiene supplies, while supporting waste management and emergency water distribution. 
  • Shelter and site management – supporting displaced families with emergency shelter, essential household items, shelter repairs, and working to strengthen the safety, dignity and environment of displacement sites. 
  • Education – providing learning opportunities and psychosocial support to children and youth who have experienced trauma and interruptions to their education through the establishment of safe learning spaces and developing the capacity of facilitators, teachers and counsellors. 
  • Protection from violence – supporting individuals and communities to prevent and respond to violence, reduce protection risks and strengthen safety, dignity and resilience. 
  • Information, counselling and legal assistance – supporting people in safeguarding their housing, land and property rights, helping to protect people from demolition, eviction and confiscation orders, as well as access restrictions, residency revocation and discrimination.

<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">
  
      <h2 class="h2 section-title red-label">Save the Children in the Occupied Palestinian Territory</h2>
    
        

<div class="text paragraph-separator">
  
            <div class="text-long"><p class="text-align-justify"><span>Save the Children has worked in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) since 1953, with a permanent presence since 1973. Since then, we have worked with partners to help provide quality education, protection for children, early childhood development support, and employment opportunities for at-risk youth. We also focus on child-centred climate change programming, advocacy and campaigning, on environmental education, community-based adaptation and climate activism.</span></p><p class="text-align-justify"><span>Operating in severe insecurity amid unprecedented levels of violence, systematic obstruction of aid by Israeli authorities, famine and the near collapse of all formal services in Gaza, as well as hostilities, continued displacement and increased settler violence in the West Bank, we have rapidly adapted our programming to remain operational and responsive. Despite the increasingly complex and evolving situation, we are doing all we can to ensure we reach children and their families. </span></p></div>
      
</div>


  </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="layout layout--onecol">
    <div class="layout__region layout__region--content">
      

<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">
  
      <h2 class="h2 section-title red-label">The situation for children in Occupied Palestinian Territory</h2>
    
        

<div class="text paragraph-separator">
  
            <div class="text-long"><p class=""><strong>Palestinian children continue to carry the weight of the occupation. </strong>Decades of conflict, the ongoing military occupation, and the blockade of Gaza hinder the right to self-determination and consequently have adverse impacts on the development of Palestinian communities, greatly increasing the vulnerability of children.</p><p class=""><strong>For too long, the occupation has denied the rights of Palestinian children and stolen their childhoods, exposing them to violence, arbitrary detentions, and cutting them off from their homes, schools and other essential services. </strong>Ultimately, the root causes of repeated bouts of violence and a decades-long child rights crisis in the oPt must be addressed. Only an end to the occupation can create the conditions for lasting peace and protection for children.</p><p class="">Palestinian children are the only children in the world who are systematically prosecuted in military courts. These courts consistently fail to offer the right to a fair trial and do not meet juvenile justice standards. Instead, it is an abusive, inhumane prosecution system, where children are being physically, emotionally and sexually abused, humiliated and starved.  </p><p class=""><strong>The widespread and systematic ill-treatment of Palestinian children within the Israeli military system is a long-standing human rights and child rights crisis.</strong> All Palestinian children arbitrarily held in Israeli military detention must be released immediately and unconditionally. No child should ever come in contact with a military court or any court that lacks comprehensive fair trial rights and basic safeguards. This decades-old protection crisis for Palestinian children has reached devastating new levels of abuse and deprivation. </p></div>
      
</div>


  </div>

<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">

  <div class="caption_text">
    <p>Nour*, 4, lost all her family in an Israeli bombing that targeted the entire block where her family lived during the early days of the war in Gaza. The bombing blew her from her family’s apartment, at a height of 30 meters, to the street, and she broke her two legs, among other injuries, on top of her pre-existing hearing and speech disability.  Shurouq Alaila/ Save the Children</p>
  </div>

<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">
  
    
          

<div class="has-grey-background text text--with-bg paragraph-separator">
  
            <div class="text-long"><h3 class="">GAZA</h3><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:12.0pt;"><strong>Tens of thousands of children have been killed by bombs and bullets. More have lost their homes and loved ones.</strong> The harm children are facing will have long-term and potentially irreversible impacts, undermining their futures and the future of Palestinian society as a whole. T<strong>he ceasefire agreement remains fragile and has shown very little respite for children and families. </strong>The implementation of the ceasefire plan <a href="https://resourcecentre.savethechildren.net/document/humanitarian-scorecard-six-months-in-gaza-ceasefire-is-failing">is failing</a>. </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:12.0pt;"><strong>The blocking of aid and goods from entering Gaza by Israeli authorities is continuing to have catastrophic impacts on children. </strong>Through the deregistration of international NGOs and existing barriers, Israeli authorities are undermining the delivery of lifesaving humanitarian assistance to children and families in oPt at a moment of unprecedented need.  </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:12.0pt;">Students and teachers <a href="https://www.savethechildren.net/stories/education-occupied-palestinian-territory-under-attack">across the oPt</a> have been killed, maimed, arrested, and detained. In Gaza, we’re at risk of seeing a “lost” generation emerge. Children are now in their third year of missing school and need to get back to the classroom, not only for their own individual development and futures but for the future of Palestinian society.  </p></div>
      
</div>


  </div>

<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">
  
    
          

<div class="has-grey-background text text--with-bg paragraph-separator">
  
            <div class="text-long"><h3 class="">THE WEST BANK</h3><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;">Every day, Palestinian children and their families are confronted with the daily violence of a military occupation.<strong> Children are forced to grow up in an asphyxiating, coercive environment</strong> marked by state-sanctioned violence, racial discrimination, the loss of loved ones, detention, and the destruction of homes and schools. These practices are strangulating the aspirations and futures of Palestinian children and devastating their mental health. </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;"> </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;">Children can't safely access education either; <strong>over 621,000 children are attending school only three times a week.</strong> Children and teachers are telling our teams they are being harassed, detained and attacked on their way to and during school, while increased checkpoints, road closures, and access impediments are severely disrupting children's access to learning.</p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;"> </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;">The siege-like tactics on communities in the West Bank are fraying the very fabric of Palestinian life and society, by separating Palestinian communities and families from each other, children from their schools and parents from their places of employment, creating conditions for Palestinians incompatible with life. Israeli forces and settlers are dismantling and obstructing vital humanitarian aid. <strong>Israeli authorities’ policies and practices are resulting in the annexation of the West Bank and violating the territorial integrity of the oPt and Palestinians’ right to self-determination.</strong>  </p></div>
      
</div>


  </div>

  <div class="caption_text">
    <p>Homes, schools, health facilities and infrastructure have been completely destroyed in Khan Younis in the Gaza Strip.

The war on Gaza since the 7 October attacks on Israel by Palestinian armed groups has resulted in horrendous consequences for children. More than 13,800 children in Gaza have been killed, as well as 106 children in the West Bank and 33 children in Israel. 

The humanitarian situation in Gaza is dire. Homes, hospitals and schools have been destroyed. More than 1.7 million people have been displaced. Now, more than one million children face the imminent threat of famine. 

Amidst extremely challenging conditions, Save the Children staff and partners have been working around the clock to support the most vulnerable children and families. Sacha Myers / Save the Children</p>

    <p>Fatima*, 40, is a mother of three.

  <div class="caption_text">
    <p>Radwa*, 30, is a mother of five from Gaza whose children face severe medical challenges worsened by the ongoing war. Her youngest daughter Basma*, 1, suffered from malnutrition after Radwa* struggled to breastfeed following major surgery and due to lack of food because of the war and siege on Gaza since 2 March. 

Save the Children provided vital support through breastfeeding support sessions, helping Radwa* continue breastfeeding Basma* and care for her children. Save the Children has also provided Ready to Use Therapeutic Food (peanut paste) for Basma* to help her recover from malnutrition. Although we were able to help Basma* this time, supplies of Ready to Use Therapeutic Food are now running out in the Gaza Strip.
 
Radwa's* eldest daughter, Mais*, 11, has a lung tumour, her son Karam*, 7, has autism and seizures.
 
Despite daily hardships and a lack of food and medical care, Radwa* remains grateful for the support that has been crucial to her children’s survival and well-being. Eyad AlTawil / Save the Children</p>

      <div><p><span lang="EN-US">Oxfam has been working in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) since the 1950s, establishing a country office in the 1980s. Together with partner organisations we work with the most vulnerable communities in Gaza and the West Bank. Our joint efforts focus on improving livelihoods and advancing the rights of communities living under illegal occupation, prolonged suffering, deprivation and hardship.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Oxfam has been delivering life‑saving humanitarian aid and programmatic support to communities across the oPt for decades. We work to facilitate humanitarian access and the delivery of assistance in line with international humanitarian law. Oxfam, together with partner organisations, responds to the humanitarian crisis with programming in areas including vital water infrastructure and other repair and maintenance work; hygiene kit distribution; livelihoods and agricultural support; food security interventions, and water sanitation and hygiene (WASH) activities. Our work also focuses on responding to needs around the protection of civilians, psycho-social support, and the rights of women.</span></p></div>

      <div><p><span lang="EN-US">Informed by partners and programmes, and founded on principles of International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law, Oxfam advocates for accountability and an immediate end to the decades-long cycle of violence in the oPt as a result of the ongoing impunity afforded to Israel, which has fueled further human rights violations, war crimes and other violations of international law.</span><br><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">The international community has failed to ensure the equal rights and self-determination of the Palestinian people as guaranteed in the UN Charter Article 1(2). Israel, as the occupying power, must uphold its obligations under international law and allow unfettered access for humanitarian relief.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">By working with coalitions to maintain pressure on key governments and international institutions, Oxfam demands that States work to ensure obligations under international humanitarian law are upheld and those violating held to account to ensure humanitarian operations can function without obstruction.</span></p></div>

      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--text paragraph--view-mode--default max-width-text mx-auto content-section-text copy-body">
  
      <div><h2><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Impacts of Israel’s illegal occupation in the oPt </strong></span><br><span lang="EN-US"></span></h2><p><span lang="EN-US">In Gaza, the combined effects of Israel's illegal occupation of the oPt (including severe restrictions on the flow of vital aid and goods, and denial of freedom of movement) continue to deepen an already severe humanitarian catastrophe. Water scarcity is escalating, with some areas of Gaza City receiving as little as two litres of drinking water per person per day.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">The overwhelming majority of Palestinians in Gaza continue to live in makeshift shelters or heavily damaged structures, facing severe shortages of food, drinking water, medical supplies, fuel, shelter materials, WASH items and cooking gas.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">From October 2023 to </span><a href="https://www.unrwa.org/resources/reports/unrwa-situation-report-225-humanitarian-crisis-gaza-strip-and-occupied-west-bank"><span lang="EN-US">June 2026,</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> amidst Israel’s ongoing genocide on Gaza, over 72,000 Palestinians were killed, and more than 173,000 injured. </span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Almost the entire population of Gaza - 2.1 million people - has been displaced, lacking access to sufficient shelter, food, life-saving medical services, clean water, education and livelihoods. In the West Bank, more than 30,000 Palestinian people have been forcibly displaced. </span></p><p><span lang="EN-GB">At the same time, the destruction of civilian infrastructure has been catastrophic: </span><a href="https://www.ochaopt.org/content/reported-impact-snapshot-gaza-strip-6-may-2026"><span lang="EN-GB">92 % of assessed commercia</span></a><span lang="EN-GB">l and industrial establishments have been destroyed or damaged. </span><a href="https://www.ochaopt.org/content/reported-impact-snapshot-gaza-strip-6-may-2026"><span lang="EN-GB">74% of the road network</span></a><span lang="EN-GB"> has been destroyed, as well as </span><a href="https://www.ochaopt.org/content/reported-impact-snapshot-gaza-strip-6-may-2026"><span lang="EN-GB">90% of energy infrastructure</span></a><span lang="EN-GB"> – including the electricity distribution network and associated assets. </span><a href="https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2024/06/states-and-companies-must-end-arms-transfers-israel-immediately-or-risk"><span lang="EN-GB">UN experts</span></a><span lang="EN-GB"> and </span><a href="https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2025/09/global-political-economy-enabling-israels-genocide-occupation-apartheid/"><span lang="EN-GB">human rights organizations</span></a><span lang="EN-GB"> have warned that companies supplying weapons or military support to Israel may risk complicity in serious violations of human rights.</span><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">In the West Bank, severe access constraints, closures and movement restrictions continue to intensify. New checkpoints and gate closures have further fragmented communities, limiting mobility for residents and humanitarian staff, yet despite the enormous challenges, Oxfam and partners continue to advance the response, sustaining coordination and scaling support where possible.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">A surge in settler violence and intensified movement restrictions is further impacting on Palestinian communities. More Palestinians have been killed by the Israeli military and settlers across the occupied West Bank in the last three years than in the previous 17 years combined.</span></p></div>
  
</div>

      <div><h2><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Oxfam position on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict</strong></span><span lang="EN-US"></span></h2><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Civilians must be protected under international law, A sustainable and just peace for Palestinians and Israelis requires ending the military occupation, addressing root causes of the conflict, and ensuring accountability for all parties. Gaza requires an immediate full and permanent ceasefire, unimpeded humanitarian access, and urgent rehabilitation of basic services.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">A permanent ceasefire in Gaza is imperative to help stop further loss of life, deliver required levels of humanitarian aid, avoid the total destruction of civic infrastructure like schools and hospitals, and cultural history. Without a permanent ceasefire, it is simply impossible for the international humanitarian system to work safely to distribute aid and help protect the lives of civilians.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">The international community must advocate towards a long-term political solution beyond humanitarian relief. This should include the dismantling of Illegal settlements, cessation of their expansion in oPt and an end to Israel's illegal military occupation, the lifting of Israeli blockade and restrictions that hamper the Palestinian economy and the movement of people and goods, and support for Palestinian self-determination and access to international forums and legal mechanisms.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">International efforts are needed now more than ever to facilitate a peace process that will lead to a viable, permanent status agreement ensuring equality, security, dignity, sovereignty, justice and prosperity, both for Palestinians and Israelis.</span></p><h2><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Oxfam’s registration in Israel</strong></span><span lang="EN-US"></span></h2><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Following the introduction of new procedures for INGO registration and the recent Israeli High Court ruling dismissing an appeal challenging these procedures from 18 humanitarian organisations including Oxfam, Oxfam is no longer registered in Israel and annexed East Jerusalem.  We continue our operations and work with our local partners in the oPt on the basis of our registration with the Palestinian Authority. </span></p></div>
  
</div>

<h2 id="stories-of-hope-wck-farmers-in-gaza" class="wp-block-heading has-h1-variant">Stories of Hope: WCK Farmers in Gaza</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Across Gaza, the land that once fed communities lies largely dormant. As of May 2025, as much as 95 percent of Gaza’s agricultural land is unusable, and 80 percent of cropland has been damaged or destroyed. Farmers—who for generations have been the backbone of Gaza’s economy and food culture—can no longer access the seeds they need. The result is felt every day in WCK’s kitchens, where fresh produce has become rare, and the meals that do include it carry an outsized meaning for displaced families.</p>

<p class="has-text-align-center wp-block-paragraph">Despite significant restrictions on humanitarian aid entering Gaza, our teams have delivered well over 100 million meals by land, sea, and air. These cookies help the website function properly, remember your preferences, understand how you engage with our content, and support our outreach efforts. Some cookies may also be used to provide a more relevant website experience. We respect your privacy and give you control over which optional cookies you allow. Select the different cookie categories below to learn more and adjust your preferences. Please note that blocking certain types of cookies may affect how the website functions or limit some features.

Please note: Using a VPN or similar service may affect how we determine your location and which cookie consent options are displayed. We encourage you to make privacy choices consistent with the laws applicable to your location.

    Politique en matière de cookies

    Lors de la navigation sur notre site, des fichiers contenant des informations, appelés « cookies », sont déposés sur votre terminal (ordinateur, smartphone, tablette ou tout autre support).

English
  • جمعية أطفالنا للصم ضمن القائمة النهائية المرشحة للفوز في الجائزة العالمية Zero Projectبترشيح من شريكنا الرئيسي مؤسسة سي
  • زيارة وفد من الاتحاد الاوروبي لجمعية أطفالنا
  • توقيع اتفاقية لتنفيذ منحة مشروع
  • زيارة وفد التعاون التنموي النمساوي وبرنامج الأمم المتحدة الإنمائي لجمعية أطفالنا
  • .

عن الجمعية

تأسست جمعية أطفالنا للصم عام 1992 في مدينة غزة بهدف مساعدة الأطفال والبالغين من ذوي الإعاقة السمعية في الحصول على فرصهم في التعليم والتأهيل والتدريب المهني. وتعتبر الجمعية المرجع الرئيس ومركزاً للموارد فيما يتعلق بالصمم لمعظم المراكز والمؤسسات والعيادات والمستشفيات العاملة في قطاع غزة، وهي عضو فعال في شبكة المنظمات الأهلية وقطاع التأهيل فيها.

 

يعمل في الجمعية أكثر من 134 موظفا وموظفة يشكل الصم منهم أكثر من 55% يعكفون جميعا على خدمة الآلاف من الأطفال والبالغين من ذوي الإعاقة وعائلاتهم الفقيرة الذين ينتفعون من برامج وخدمات الجمعية المتنوعة، تبنت الجمعية منذ العام 2017 النهج التنموي الشامل في تقديم خدماتها لضمان فرص متساوية ومجتمع متاح لجميع أفراده بما فيهم الأشخاص من ذوي الإعاقة السمعية .

خدماتنا

تهدف الجمعية إلى تحسين جودة حياة الأطفال والبالغين من ذوي الإعاقة السمعية من خلال تزويدهم بالخدمات التعليمية والصحية والاجتماعية عالية الجودة وخلق فرص عمل كريمة لهم.
 
 

برنامج لغة الإشارة

يقدم برنامج لغة الإشارة خدماته لجميع فئات المجتمع وخاصة للأفراد من ذوي الإعاقة السمعية وأسرهم وعائلاتهم الممتدة والعاملين في مؤسسات المجتمع المدني.

 

برنامج التدخل المبكر

يسعى برنامج التدخل المبكر لمساعدة أهالي الأطفال الذين تم تشخيص الصمم لديهم حديثاً وفق خطط فردية خاصة بكل طفل

 

المدرسة

تتضمن المدرسة تسعة مستويات تعليمية تبدأ بالصف الأول وتنتهي بالصف التاسع، وتعتمد منهجية التعليم فيها على ثنائية اللغة.

 

الروضة

تعتمد الروضة على منهج التعلم عن طريق اللعب والزوايا التعليمية، حيث تهدف إلى إحداث تغيرات إيجابية في توجهات الأطفال وهواياتهم وعاداتهم ومهاراتهم وقدراتهم

 

برنامج التدريب المهني

يقدم برنامج التدريب المهني دورات تدريبية مهنية قصيرة وطويلة الأمد في مجالات عدة وتشمل: التصميم والخياطة والتطريز والنجارة والأثاث والتنجيد والرسم على الخشب وصناعة الفخار والسيراميك والأرابيسك.

 

عيادة السمعيات

تقدم عيادة السمعيات خدماتها لجميع أفراد المجتمع المحلي حيث يعمل في العيادة أخصائيو سمعيات مؤهلون في مجالات تقييم وتشخيص مشاكل السمع وتركيب السماعات الطبية.

 

المركز المجتمعي لتعليم الكباء

يقدم المركز المجتمعي لتعليم الكباء خدمات التعليم والتدريب التقني والمهني وبناء المهارات الوظيفية وفق حاجات سوق العمل المحلي.

 

قسم الانتاج الحرفي

• يشمل قسم الانتاج الحرفي على ورش للإنتاج كالمنجرة وورش الخياطة والتطريز وصناعة الفخار والسيراميك والرسم على الخشب وحياكة البسط ونسج القماش المجدلاوي.

قصتنا

أسست جمعية نجوم الأمل لتمكين النساء ذوات الإعاقة علي يد نخبة من النساء ذوات الاعاقة عام 2007، إيمانًا منهن بالحاجة الملحة لوجود منظمة تتفرد في تلبية احتياجات النساء والفتيات ذوات الإعاقة؛ نظرًا لحجم التمييز والعنف المضاعف عليهن بفعل كونهن نساء من جهة وذوات إعاقة من جهة أخرى.

 

تعمل الجمعية على إلغاء العنف الواقع على النساء ذوات الإعاقة بتقدميها خدمات تتنوع بين التوعية، والارشاد، التمكين ل:

1- النساء والفتيات ذوات الإعاقة أنفسهن وذويهن.

2- صناع القرار على المستوى السياسي والمؤسسي.

١١ نوفمبر ٢٠٢٦

الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين تُطلق مبادرة إنسانية لحلاقة وتجهيز الأطفال من ذوي الإعاقة

وثقت الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين عبر مقطع مرئي جديد جانباً من فعاليات مبادرتها الميدانية المخصصة لحلاقة وتجهيز الأطفال من ذوي الإعاقة. وتهدف المبادرة إلى تقديم خدمات العناية الشخصية للأطفال في بيئة صديقة ومحفزة تراعي احتياجاتهم الخاصة وتخفف الأعباء النفسية والاقتصادية عن كاهل عائلاتهم، وذلك بمشاركة نخبة من المتطوعين المختصين بكوادر الجمعية. وتؤكد الجمعية أن هذه المبادرة تأتي ضمن سلسلة من البرامج والخدمات التأهيلية الموجهة لدعم الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة وتعزيز دمجهم ومساندتهم في المجتمع بكل كرامة واهتمام. [شاهد الفيديو أعلاه] 🔻 للمساهمة في رعاية البرامج والمشاريع القادمة للأطفال، يمكنكم التبرع مباشرة عبر صفحة المبادرات https://pardgaza.ps/donate.

اقرأ التفاصيل
فيديو
٢٦ أكتوبر ٢٠٢٦

زيتونُنا هُويّتنا وفنُّنا حكايةُ انتمائنا: إبداعات الطلاب في مادة التربية الفنية

توثيق نتاجات مادة التربية الفنية لطلاب الجمعية وترسيخ الهوية والتراث الفلسطيني من خلال الرسم. تحت شعار «زيتونُنا هُويّتنا… وفنُّنا حكايةُ انتمائنا»، نظمت الجمعية نشاطاً فنياً ضمن مادة التربية الفنية بالتزامن مع موسم قطف الزيتون. هدف النشاط إلى إتاحة المساحة للطلاب للتعبير عن مشاعرهم وارتباطهم بأرضهم وتراثهم عبر أدوات الرسم والألوان، لترسيخ المفاهيم الوطنية والجمالية في نفوسهم. ندعوكم لمشاهدة المقطع التوثيقي المرفق للاطلاع على إبداعات رسامينا الصغار.

نظمت الجمعية الفلسطينية، بالتنسيق والتعاون مع وكالة غوث وتشغيل اللاجئين الفلسطينيين (الأونروا)، ورشة عمل تدريبية استهدفت المعلمات؛ بهدف تعزيز قدراتهن على التحديد والاكتشاف المبكر للحالات الحرجـة التي تتطلب تدخلاً متخصصاً، وتوضيح مسارات ومعايير الإحالة المعتمدة للتعامل معها وفق الأصول والبرامج المعمول بها في الأونروا.

برامج ومشاريع الجمعية

نسعى من خلال مجموعة متكاملة من البرامج والمشاريع لتلبية احتياجات الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة وتوفير الرعاية الشاملة لهم ولأسرهم.

برنامج المدرسة - التأهيل المهني

تدريب مهني متخصص يهدف إلى تمكين الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة من اكتساب مهارات عملية تساعدهم على الاستقلالية والاندماج في سوق العمل.

برنامج المدرسة - التعليم الأكاديمي

برنامج تعليمي شامل يوفر تعليماً أكاديمياً متميزاً للطلاب ذوي الاحتياجات الخاصة وفق منهاج وزارة التربية والتعليم الفلسطينية.

مركز تعزيز القدرات

برامج متنوعة لتطوير المهارات الحياتية والاجتماعية والنفسية للأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة وأسرهم من خلال ورش عمل وأنشطة تفاعلية.

اقرأ المزيد

البرنامج الخارجي

خدمات تأهيلية منزلية ومجتمعية تصل إلى الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة في منازلهم ومجتمعاتهم المحلية لضمان وصول الخدمة للجميع.

اقرأ المزيد

وحدة العلاج الطبيعي

خدمات علاج طبيعي متخصصة تقدمها كوادر مؤهلة باستخدام أحدث التقنيات والأجهزة لتحسين الحركة والوظائف الجسدية.

اقرأ المزيد

برامج الدعم الأسري

دعم نفسي واجتماعي لأسر الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة من خلال جلسات إرشادية ومجموعات دعم لتعزيز قدرتهم على الرعاية والتعامل.

اقرأ المزيد
المشروع الأبرز حالياً

مشروع دعم وتوفير احتياجات المعاقين في قطاع غزة

    function dataTable(wrap) {

        if (!table) return;
        var heads = [];
        table.querySelectorAll('thead tr:last-child th, thead tr:last-child td').forEach(function (th) {
            var label = th.hasAttribute('data-label') ? th.getAttribute('data-label') : th.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();

            Array.prototype.forEach.call(tr.children, function (td) {

        .hub-hero h1 {

        /* ===============================
           NEWS TICKER — شريط الأخبار
           ===============================
           لا marquee أفقي: النصّ المتحرّك أفقياً يصعب لحاقه بالعربية، ولا يمكن
           النقر على هدف يتحرّك، ويتعذّر إيقافه لمن يحتاج. البديل سطر ثابت
           المكان يتبدّل محتواه رأسياً كل 6 ثوانٍ، ويتوقّف عند التحويم أو التركيز. */
        .news-ticker {
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.85rem;
            width: 100%; margin-bottom: 1.5rem;
            padding: 0.7rem 1.1rem;
            background: rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
            backdrop-filter: blur(14px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(14px);
            border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.10);
            border-radius: 14px;
            cursor: pointer; text-align: right;
            font-family: 'Rubik', Arial, sans-serif;
            transition: background 0.3s ease, border-color 0.3s ease;
            opacity: 0; animation: fadeUp 0.6s ease 0.1s forwards;
            position: relative; overflow: hidden;
        }
        .news-ticker:hover, .news-ticker:focus-visible {
            background: rgba(255,255,255,0.1);
            border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.18);
        }
        .news-ticker:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--sdf-amber); outline-offset: 2px; }
        .nt-label {
            display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; flex-shrink: 0;
            color: var(--sdf-amber); font-size: 0.76rem; font-weight: 600;
            padding-left: 0.85rem; border-left: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);
        }
        .nt-label i { font-size: 0.95rem; }
        .nt-viewport { flex: 1; min-width: 0; position: relative; height: 22px; }
        .nt-item {
            position: absolute; inset: 0;
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6rem;
            opacity: 0; transform: translateY(100%);
            transition: opacity 0.45s ease, transform 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1);
            pointer-events: none;
        }
        .nt-item.is-active { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
        .nt-item.is-out { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-100%); }
        .nt-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; flex-shrink: 0; }
        .nt-title {
            color: var(--ink-95); font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 500;
            white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
        }
        .nt-type { color: var(--ink-40); font-size: 0.72rem; flex-shrink: 0; }
        .nt-ago  { color: var(--ink-30); font-size: 0.7rem; flex-shrink: 0; margin-right: auto; padding-right: 0.6rem; }
        .nt-new {
            flex-shrink: 0; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px;
            background: rgba(255,152,51,0.16); border: 1px solid rgba(255,152,51,0.3);
            color: #ffc78a; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 600;
            padding: 3px 10px; border-radius: 20px;
        }
        .nt-new-dot {
            width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--sdf-orange);
            animation: ntPulse 2s ease-in-out infinite;
        }
        @keyframes ntPulse { 0%,100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.35; } }
        .nt-pips { display: flex; gap: 4px; flex-shrink: 0; }
        .nt-pip {
            width: 5px; height: 5px; border-radius: 50%;
            background: rgba(255,255,255,0.2); transition: background 0.3s, width 0.3s;
        }
        .nt-pip.is-active { background: var(--sdf-amber); width: 14px; border-radius: 3px; }
        .nt-caret { color: var(--ink-30); font-size: 1.1rem; flex-shrink: 0; }
        .news-ticker.is-empty { cursor: default; }

        /* --- Updates drawer --- */
        .nd-backdrop {
            position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 1200;
            background: rgba(6,15,20,0.55);
            backdrop-filter: blur(2px);
            opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; transition: opacity 0.3s ease;
        }
        .nd-backdrop.is-open { opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto; }
        .news-drawer {
            position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; z-index: 1201;
            width: 400px; max-width: 92vw;
            background: linear-gradient(170deg, #122733 0%, #16303f 100%);
            border-left: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
            box-shadow: -20px 0 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);
            transform: translateX(100%); transition: transform 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1);
            display: flex; flex-direction: column; direction: rtl;
        }

        .nd-head {
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6rem;
            padding: 1.1rem 1.25rem; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
        }
        .nd-head h4 {
            font-family: 'Alexandria','Rubik',sans-serif;
            color: var(--ink-95); font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; margin: 0;
        }
        .nd-head-count {

        }
        .nd-close {
            margin-right: auto; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.06);

            display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
            font-size: 1.1rem; transition: all 0.25s ease;
        }
        .nd-close:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.14); color: #fff; }
        .nd-list { flex: 1; overflow-y: auto; padding: 0.75rem; }
        .nd-card {
            display: block; text-decoration: none;
            background: rgba(255,255,255,0.045);
            border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.07);
            border-right: 3px solid var(--nd-accent, #64748B);
            border-radius: 12px; padding: 0.9rem 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.65rem;
            transition: all 0.25s ease;
        }
        .nd-card:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.09); border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.14); text-decoration: none; }
        .nd-card-top { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.35rem; }
        .nd-card-type {
            font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 600; padding: 2px 9px; border-radius: 6px;
            /* اسم المشروع قد يكون طويلاً جداً فيبتلع سطر الترويسة كاملاً */
            max-width: 62%; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
        }
        .nd-card-ago { color: var(--ink-30); font-size: 0.68rem; margin-right: auto; flex-shrink: 0; }
        .nd-card h5 {
            color: var(--ink-95); font-size: 0.88rem; font-weight: 600; margin: 0 0 0.3rem; line-height: 1.5;
            display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;
        }
        .nd-card p {
            color: var(--ink-40); font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.7; margin: 0;
            display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;
        }
        .nd-card-foot { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; margin-top: 0.55rem; }
        .nd-card-author { color: var(--ink-30); font-size: 0.7rem; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; }
        .nd-card-author img { width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; object-fit: cover; }
        .nd-unread-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--sdf-orange); flex-shrink: 0; }
        .nd-foot { padding: 0.85rem 1.25rem; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); }
        .nd-foot a {
            display: block; text-align: center; text-decoration: none;
            background: rgba(255,255,255,0.07); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1);
            color: var(--ink-60); font-size: 0.78rem; padding: 9px; border-radius: 9px;
            transition: all 0.25s ease;
        }
        .nd-foot a:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.13); color: #fff; text-decoration: none; }
        .nd-empty { text-align: center; padding: 3rem 1.5rem; color: var(--ink-30); }
        .nd-empty i { font-size: 2.4rem; display: block; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; opacity: 0.6; }
        .nd-empty p { font-size: 0.82rem; }

        /* --- «يلا راديو»: صفّ واحد هادئ بأسلوب بطاقة بلبل ---
           الصوت في نافذة /radio المنفصلة كي لا يتوقف عند التنقّل؛ هذه ريموت فقط.
           الموجة وأدوات الصوت لا تظهر إلا أثناء البثّ حتى لا تزدحم الصفحة. */
        .rc {
            --teal: #1CB7B3; --teal2: #57D3D0; --on-teal: #06231F; --idle: #2A3A5A;
            margin-top: 0.9rem; padding: 0.9rem 1rem; border-radius: 16px;
            background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(28,183,179,0.13), rgba(24,24,24,0.5));
            border: 1px solid rgba(28,183,179,0.24);
            transition: border-color 0.35s ease, box-shadow 0.35s ease;
            font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
        }
        .rc.is-on { border-color: rgba(28,183,179,0.45); box-shadow: 0 12px 30px rgba(28,183,179,0.14); }
        .rc input[type=range] { accent-color: var(--teal); }
        .rc-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.8rem; }
        .rc-tile {
            --punch: 0; width: 42px; height: 42px; border-radius: 12px; flex-shrink: 0; background: #181818;
            display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: var(--teal);
            transform: scale(calc(1 + var(--punch) * 0.05));
            box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgba(28,183,179,0.22);
        }
        .rc.is-muted .rc-tile { color: var(--idle); }
        .rc-tile svg { width: 22px; height: 22px; }
        .rc-info { min-width: 0; flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.15rem; }
        .rc-title { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink-95); }
        .rc-title i { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: #6F7F98; flex-shrink: 0; }
        .rc.is-on .rc-title i { background: #dc2626; animation: rcPulse 1.6s ease-in-out infinite; }
        @keyframes rcPulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); } 50% { opacity: .45; transform: scale(.82); } }
        .rc-state { font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 300; color: var(--ink-40); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }
        .rc-play {
            width: 38px; height: 38px; border-radius: 50%; flex-shrink: 0; border: 0; cursor: pointer;
            background: var(--teal); color: var(--on-teal); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
            transition: background .2s, transform .12s;
        }
        .rc-play:hover { background: var(--teal2); }
        .rc-play:active { transform: scale(0.94); }
        .rc-play svg { width: 14px; height: 14px; }
        .rc-open {
            width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 9px; flex-shrink: 0; cursor: pointer;
            border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12); background: transparent; color: var(--ink-40);
            display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; transition: border-color .2s, color .2s;
        }
        .rc-open:hover { border-color: rgba(28,183,179,0.5); color: var(--teal2); }
        .rc-open svg { width: 13px; height: 13px; }
        /* لا تظهر إلا أثناء البثّ */
        .rc-more { max-height: 0; opacity: 0; overflow: hidden; transition: max-height .35s ease, opacity .3s ease, margin-top .35s ease; }
        .rc.is-live .rc-more { max-height: 90px; opacity: 1; margin-top: 0.7rem; }
        .rc-viz { display: block; width: 100%; height: 26px; margin-bottom: 6px; }
        .rc-vol { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; }
        .rc-ico {
            width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 8px; flex-shrink: 0; cursor: pointer;
            border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12); background: transparent; color: var(--ink-40);
            display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; transition: border-color .2s, color .2s, transform .12s;
        }
        .rc-ico:hover { border-color: rgba(28,183,179,0.5); color: var(--teal2); }
        .rc-ico:active { transform: scale(0.92); }
        .rc-ico[aria-pressed="true"] { color: #FF8A8A; border-color: rgba(220,38,38,0.4); }
        .rc-ico svg { width: 14px; height: 14px; }
        .rc-range { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
        .rc-pct { width: 26px; text-align: left; font-size: 0.68rem; color: var(--ink-40); flex-shrink: 0; }
        .rc-play:focus-visible, .rc-ico:focus-visible, .rc-range:focus-visible, .rc-open:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--teal); outline-offset: 2px; }
        @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
            .rc-tile, .rc.is-on .rc-title i { animation: none !important; transform: none !important; }
        }

        /* --- Bulbul (AI assistant) --- */
        .bulbul-card {
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.8rem;
            margin-top: 0.9rem; padding: 0.9rem 1rem;
            background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(124,58,237,0.16), rgba(24,24,24,0.5));
            border: 1px solid rgba(167,139,250,0.28);

            transition: all 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1);

        }
        .bulbul-card:hover {
            transform: translateY(-3px);
            border-color: rgba(167,139,250,0.5);
            box-shadow: 0 14px 34px rgba(124,58,237,0.22);
            text-decoration: none;
        }
        .bulbul-avatar {
            width: 42px; height: 42px; border-radius: 12px; flex-shrink: 0;

        .bulbul-info h4 { color: var(--ink-95); font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 0.15rem; }
        .bulbul-info p { color: var(--ink-40); font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 300; }

        .main-portal-card h3 {
            font-family: 'Alexandria', 'Rubik', sans-serif;

        .main-portal-card p { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.66); font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 300; margin-bottom: 1.25rem; line-height: 1.7; }
        .main-portal-badge {
            display: inline-block; padding: 5px 16px; border-radius: 20px;
            background: rgba(255,152,51,0.12); border: 1px solid rgba(255,152,51,0.2);
            color: rgba(255,190,100,0.9); font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 500;
        }

        .hub-secondary { flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; min-width: 0; }
        .hub-section-label {
            display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6rem;
            color: rgba(255,255,255,0.55); font-size: 0.74rem; font-weight: 400;
            opacity: 0; animation: fadeUp 0.5s ease 0.2s forwards;
        }
        .hub-section-label::after {
            content: ''; flex: 1; height: 1px;
            background: linear-gradient(-90deg, transparent, rgba(255,255,255,0.08));
        }
        .hub-section-label i { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.25); }
        .secondary-grid {
            display: grid;
            grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(230px, 1fr));
            gap: 0.9rem;
        }
        .secondary-card {
            background: var(--glass);
            backdrop-filter: blur(14px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(14px);
            border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.07);

            transition: all 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);

        .secondary-card:nth-child(1) { animation-delay: 0.25s; }
        .secondary-card:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 0.32s; }
        .secondary-card:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 0.39s; }
        .secondary-card:nth-child(4) { animation-delay: 0.46s; }
        .secondary-card:nth-child(5) { animation-delay: 0.53s; }
        .secondary-card:nth-child(6) { animation-delay: 0.6s; }
        .secondary-card:nth-child(7) { animation-delay: 0.67s; }
        .secondary-card:nth-child(8) { animation-delay: 0.74s; }
        .secondary-card::after {

            border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.12);

            width: 46px; height: 46px; border-radius: 13px;

function toggleLayout() {
    var current = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-layout');
    if (current === 'horizontal') {
        localStorage.setItem('sdf-layout', 'vertical');
    } else {
        localStorage.setItem('sdf-layout', 'horizontal');
    }
    window.location.reload();
}

function updateLayoutIcon() {
    var current = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-layout');
    var iconEl = document.getElementById('layout-toggle-icon');
    var btnEl = document.getElementById('layout-toggle-btn');
    if (iconEl) {
        iconEl.className = (current === 'horizontal')
            ? 'bx bx-layout fs-22'
            : 'bx bx-grid-alt fs-22';
    }
    if (btnEl) {
        btnEl.title = (current === 'horizontal')
            ? 'Switch to Vertical Menu'
            : 'Switch to Horizontal Menu';
    }
}

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', updateLayoutIcon);

✨ رسالة الإدارة

نحو مستقبل أكثر شمولًا وتمكينًا للأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة البصرية

انطلاقًا من إيماننا الراسخ بأهمية تمكين الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة البصرية وتعزيز حقوقهم، نواصل العمل في جمعية منتدى غزة لذوي الإعاقة البصرية الخيرية في سبيل تقديم الخدمات والبرامج التي تسهم في دعم الأشخاص المكفوفين وضعاف البصر، وتعزيز قدرتهم على الوصول إلى التعليم والرعاية الصحية والدعم النفسي والاجتماعي والتأهيل، بما يضمن لهم حياة كريمة ومشاركة فاعلة في المجتمع.

وقد حرصنا منذ تأسيس الجمعية على العمل بالشراكة والتعاون مع المؤسسات المحلية والدولية والجهات ذات العلاقة، والاستجابة للاحتياجات المتزايدة للأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة البصرية، لا سيما في ظل الظروف الإنسانية الصعبة التي يعيشها قطاع غزة.

وإذ نؤكد التزامنا بمواصلة العمل لخدمة هذه الفئة، فإننا نثمّن جهود جميع العاملين والمتطوعين والشركاء والداعمين، ونؤمن بأن العمل المشترك والمسؤولية المجتمعية يشكلان أساسًا لبناء مستقبل أكثر شمولًا وإنصافًا للأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة البصرية.

نسأل الله أن يوفقنا جميعًا لما فيه الخير، وأن نستمر في أداء رسالتنا الإنسانية والمجتمعية بكل أمانة ومسؤولية.

برامجنا ومشاريعنا

نعمل على تنفيذ برامج ومشاريع متخصصة تهدف إلى دعم وتمكين الأشخاص المكفوفين وضعاف البصر، وتعزيز حقهم في التعليم والصحة والتأهيل والمشاركة المجتمعية، بما يسهم في بناء حياة أكثر استقلالية وكرامة.

التأهيل والإرشاد الحركي

يهدف إلى دعم الأشخاص المكفوفين وضعاف البصر من خلال خدمات التأهيل والإرشاد الحركي، بما يساعدهم على تطوير مهارات التنقل الآمن والمستقل، واستخدام العصا البيضاء ووسائل الحركة المساعدة، والتعرّف على الطرق والبيئة المحيطة، بما يعزز استقلاليتهم وثقتهم بأنفسهم ويسهم في اندماجهم في المجتمع.

التعليم الشامل والدامج

يهدف إلى دعم حق الأشخاص المكفوفين وضعاف البصر في الحصول على تعليم شامل ودامج، من خلال توفير الدعم التعليمي والوسائل المساندة، وتعزيز قدرات الطلبة وأسرهم والكوادر التعليمية، بما يسهم في تهيئة بيئة تعليمية أكثر وصولًا وإنصافًا، وتعزيز فرص التعلم والمشاركة والاستقلالية.

التأهيل النفسي والاجتماعي

يهدف إلى تقديم الدعم النفسي والاجتماعي للأشخاص المكفوفين وضعاف البصر وأسرهم، من خلال جلسات فردية وجماعية وأنشطة داعمة تساعد على تعزيز الصحة النفسية، والتكيف مع الظروف الصعبة، وبناء القدرة على مواجهة التحديات، بما يسهم في تعزيز اندماجهم ومشاركتهم في المجتمع.

التدريب والتمكين

يهدف إلى تطوير مهارات وقدرات الأشخاص المكفوفين وضعاف البصر من خلال برامج تدريبية وتأهيلية متنوعة، بما يعزز استقلاليتهم وثقتهم بأنفسهم، ويدعم فرصهم في التعليم والعمل والمشاركة الفاعلة في المجتمع.

الرعاية الطبية

يهدف إلى توفير خدمات الرعاية الصحية الأساسية للأشخاص المكفوفين وضعاف البصر، بما يشمل الفحص الطبي، والتوعية الصحية، والعلاج والأدوية، بما يسهم في تحسين صحتهم وجودة حياتهم وتعزيز وصولهم إلى الخدمات الصحية بشكل آمن وميسّر.

من المجتمع ولدنا .. ولاجله نعمل.
